narration.text: So, as we just saw, the world of supervised learning basically splits into two main paths.
When a new, white test point appears in the middle, the model has to answer it.
Imagine a graph with two distinct clusters: red dots on one side and blue dots on the other. The model draws a boundary line — a decision border.
As that test point moves slightly across the line, the model assigns it a color. It is essentially asking: which group does this belong to?
Now, let's shift our focus to Regression. Here, we are not picking from a list of labels. We are predicting a continuous value.
Think of a scatter plot where the x-axis represents study hours and the y-axis represents marks. Instead of a boundary line, we see a trend line fitting through the dots.
When a new value for study hours appears, we follow a vertical line up to that trend line and read off the predicted score on the y-axis.
To put it simply, Classification asks, which class? Regression asks, what value? One is about grouping, the other is about measuring.

notes.tone: Premium, restrained, geometric, and continuous. The scene should feel like one system being interpreted in two different ways.
